Independent direct bounded enumeration and rational integration
correctness.rationale: An Abelian border longer than half the word gives a complementary shorter one by subtracting Parikh vectors. A longer-than-one factor with equal ends is bordered at length one. The one-marker factors with unequal ends have no Abelian border. For a two-marker factor 0ʲ10ᵇ1, when j>b every prefix of length at most half contains no marker and the matching suffix contains one; when j≤b, 0ʲ1 is itself a literal border. Reversal gives the other side. This proves the disjoint factor set and U=2+2T for m≥1; for 11 only the single-letter word 1 qualifies. The balanced triples attain the lower bound, and T=m occurs exactly when b=0 or b=m. Fixing b between ceil((m−t)/2) and t then counting pairs a+c=m−b with both at most t gives the finite CDF. The normalized simplex slice at b/m=B has length (1−B)−2max(1−B−x,0), on (1−x)/2≤B≤x. Integrating against normalized area gives the two stated pieces. The moments are correct: the tail integrals on [1/3,1] yield 1/3 and 13/36 and must be augmented by 1/3 and 1/9 from [0,1/3], respectively; line 91 omits that interval in its wording. The corrected integrals give 2/3 and 17/36, hence variance 1/36. The statistic and its square are Lipschitz on the simplex, so boundary-grid and interior quadrature errors are O(1/m), giving the stated rates after rescaling. Independent bounded checking constructed every substring, tested equal-length prefix/suffix Parikh vectors, and compared deduplicated sets, CDF counts, extrema and maximum multiplicities for all 1,771 gap triples with m≤20.
residual_risks: The moment-integration sentence has an omitted interval but no moment value or finding requires alteration.
The finite enumeration does not prove any of the all-length or limiting assertions. The word and factor sampling conventions must not be interchanged.

checked_sources: Frozen exact factor count, extrema and distribution
value.rationale: Weight two is a natural first case with two competing marker separations and orientation-dependent factors. The per-word exact diversity, rather than global existence of borders, identifies a genuine boundary between diversity controlled by one gap and by a+c−b. The census gives fully classified extrema and a nondegenerate law under a natural fixed-composition random model. These results are useful benchmarks for sparse-word factor diversity even though the individual border test reduces to the ordinary one.
residual_risks: No extension to more than two markers, to cyclic factors or to occurrence-weighted factors is established.
